prompt: Synthesize the interview notes below into root-cause findings for a rise in plant safety incidents, and recommend the priority fix.
context: Plant manager: "Incident count is up from 2/quarter to 7/quarter this year, mostly minor (no lost-time injuries yet)." Safety officer: "Most of the recent incidents happened on the night shift." Night-shift supervisor: "We're running with 2 fewer experienced technicians than day shift after 2 retirements this year — we backfilled with newer hires but haven't finished cross-training them on all stations." Day-shift technician (transferred briefly to night shift to help): "The safety-checklist sign-off on night shift felt rushed compared to how we do it on days — I think because they're short-staffed and behind on output targets."

binaryCriteria.description: Builds an explicit causal chain connecting the night-shift concentration, the staffing/cross-training gap, and the rushed safety-checklist behavior, rather than listing them as separate, unconnected observations.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer states "incidents are higher on night shift" without explaining why using the staffing and checklist evidence.

binaryCriteria.description: Identifies the loss of 2 experienced technicians and incomplete cross-training of their replacements as the root trigger of the chain, not just a contributing detail.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the staffing/cross-training gap is omitted from the root-cause findings.

binaryCriteria.description: Recommends addressing the staffing/cross-training gap directly as the priority fix, rather than only recommending generic "more safety training" or "reinforce safety culture".
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the recommendation is limited to generic safety-culture messaging without addressing the specific staffing/cross-training shortfall.

goldNotes: A strong synthesis identifies that the incident increase is concentrated on night shift (per the safety officer) and connects this directly to two compounding factors from the other interviews: (1) a experience/staffing gap (2 fewer experienced technicians, incomplete cross-training of newer hires) and (2) a resulting process shortcut (rushed safety-checklist sign-off, explicitly linked by the transferred day-shift technician to being short-staffed and behind on output targets) — these are not independent findings but a causal chain (staffing gap -> time pressure -> rushed safety compliance -> more incidents). A weak synthesis lists "night shift has more incidents" as if that were itself an explanation, without identifying why, or treats the staffing gap and the rushed-checklist observation as unrelated. The priority fix should address the staffing/cross-training gap directly (since it is the root trigger of the causal chain), not just "reinforce safety training" in the abstract, which would treat a symptom (rushed compliance) rather than the cause (being short-staffed and behind on training).
